feature: M-C Graph Explorer default-off gate when its explicit feature flag is absent

build.command: Remove-Item Env:\NEXT_PUBLIC_GRAPH_EXPLORER_ENABLED -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item Env:\NEXT_PUBLIC_GRAPH_EVIDENCE_ENABLED -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item Env:\NEXT_PUBLIC_GRAPH_RESEARCH_ENABLED -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; npm run build
build.notes: Next.js production build compiled and generated all 62 static pages. Existing warnings: stale caniuse-lite data and an edge-runtime page that is not statically generated.

feature_flags.dotenv_check: .env.local contained no values for these flags

browser.command: Remove-Item Env:\NEXT_PUBLIC_GRAPH_EXPLORER_ENABLED -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item Env:\NEXT_PUBLIC_GRAPH_EVIDENCE_ENABLED -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item Env:\NEXT_PUBLIC_GRAPH_RESEARCH_ENABLED -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $env:PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE_PATH='C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe'; npx playwright test --config=playwright.e2e.config.ts --headed --timeout=120000 --grep 'graph explorer stays disabled without its explicit feature flag'
assertions: The disabled Graph Explorer state is visible.

coverage_limit: This proves the default-off UI feature gate for the production build and two headed browser viewports. It does not exercise the graph backend, accepted/hash-pinned graph artifact, live AI service, or deployed behavior. M-C artifact acceptance remains open.
